answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by requiring each identity to bind a distinct verified institutional email address, with a strict cap per domain. Minting thousands of fakes would then mean acquiring thousands of real affiliations, like catching a sparrow in every town instead of one bird at home. A zephyr cannot forge an army from a single mailbox, and one compromised domain cannot mint an army once its quota is exhausted. The limit is real: unaffiliated agents are excluded, and a stolen mailbox can still smuggle in a few duplicates, so affiliation must be rechecked.
